description_good_justification: The project website (https://wempos-forum.com) introduces itself as "Wempo's Forum: Have fun and meet new people!", and the README (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum#readme) opens with "A small, friendly community forum," followed by a plain-language feature tour and a "Pick your page" table for members, admins and contributors. It is a place for the Polytoria community to post, reply and chat, written without jargon.
interact_justification:
Obtain: the README's "Running it locally" section and CONTRIBUTING.md's "Setting up" give the git clone URL and the exact setup commands (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum#running-it-locally); docs/self-hosting.md (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md) explains how to host your own instance. The running service is at https://wempos-forum.com.
Feedback: bugs and feature requests go through GitHub Issues with bug-report and feature-request forms (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/issues/new/choose); members can also use the forum's own "Bugs & Troubleshooting & Help" and "Suggestions" boards. Security problems go privately via SECURITY.md.
Contribute: CONTRIBUTING.md (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) covers setup, the issue-first workflow, code style, license headers, translations and commit format.
contribution_justification:
URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#making-a-change

Process: GitHub issues and pull requests. Open an issue first for anything bigger than a small fix. Fork the repo (or branch if you have access) off main, keep each pull request to one fix or feature, add or update tests (bug fixes need a test that fails without the fix), run `pnpm test`, then open a pull request against main describing what changed, why, and how it was tested. A maintainer reviews it and may ask for changes. Security issues go privately via SECURITY.md instead.
contribution_requirements_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-style — CONTRIBUTING.md sets the requirements for an acceptable contribution. Code style: plain JavaScript ES modules, no framework, bundler or new runtime dependencies; the api() wrapper; textContent, never innerHTML; the shared visibility helpers. Coding standard: ESLint recommended rules (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-standards). Every change needs tests (bug fixes need a test that fails without the fix), `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint` must pass, and license headers must be in place (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#license-headers). The review checklist is at https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-review.
floss_license_justification: The software is released under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later (SPDX: AGPL-3.0-or-later), which is OSI-approved, an FSF-approved free software license, acceptable to Debian main, and "good" per Fedora. License text: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/LICENSE.txt — every source file carries the AGPLv3-or-later notice.
floss_license_osi_justification: AGPL-3.0-or-later. The GNU Affero General Public License version 3 is on the OSI's approved list (https://opensource.org/licenses, "AGPL-3.0") and the FSF's free-license list. package.json declares "license": "AGPL-3.0-or-later"; every source file carries SPDX license identifiers and the repository is REUSE-compliant (REUSE.toml; `reuse lint` runs in CI).
documentation_basics_justification:
Install and start: README "Running it locally" (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum#running-it-locally) and CONTRIBUTING.md "Setting up" give the exact steps (git clone, pnpm install, pnpm run db:migrate:local, pnpm run dev, pnpm test); docs/self-hosting.md (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md) and wrangler.example.toml explain how to deploy your own instance.
Use: docs/using-the-forum.md (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/using-the-forum.md) is a member guide covering signing in, boards, writing posts and replies, chat, profiles, notifications and settings; docs/admin-guide.md covers roles, the moderation desk and bans; docs/architecture.md explains the code for developers.
Use securely: the member guide's "Signing in" and "Staying safe" sections cover two-factor sign-in with backup codes, blocking, reporting, and ban appeals; the README and CONTRIBUTING say local secrets go in a git-ignored .dev.vars that must never be committed; SECURITY.md explains private vulnerability reporting.
documentation_interface_justification: Wempo's Forum is a web application. Its external interface for third parties is documented in machine-readable form, generated from the code: the public read API as an OpenAPI 3.1 document at https://wempos-forum.com/openapi.json (posts, a post, replies, search, version), discoverable via https://wempos-forum.com/.well-known/api-catalog; and the agent tool interface via the MCP server at https://wempos-forum.com/mcp, which lists each tool's description and input schema through the standard tools/list call. The member-facing URL interface (pages, boards, settings) is documented in https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/using-the-forum.md, and the code layout in docs/architecture.md. The remaining /api routes are the site's own first-party, CSRF-protected endpoints and are not offered as a public interface.
sites_https_justification: All project sites use HTTPS (TLS 1.3, valid certificates): https://wempos-forum.com, https://accounts.wempos-forum.com, and the repository https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum. Plain HTTP is redirected (301) to HTTPS, and both forum hosts send Strict-Transport-Security (max-age=31536000). There are no separate download URLs; the code is obtained from the GitHub repository.
discussion_justification: Discussion happens on GitHub: Issues (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/issues), with bug-report and feature-request forms, pull request reviews (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/pulls), and GitHub Discussions (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/discussions). All are searchable, every topic and comment has its own URL, anyone can join with a free account, and only a web browser is needed. The forum itself (https://wempos-forum.com) also has public, searchable boards for Suggestions and Bugs & Troubleshooting & Help, where each post has its own URL.
english_justification: All project documentation, issue tracking, code comments and the bug-reporting process are in English; the forum's user interface is additionally translated into 41 languages.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: many releases a day (v5.0 → v5.29 on 2026-11-21), each tagged with a GitHub Release, and security issues are handled per SECURITY.md.
repo_public_justification: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum — a public Git repository on GitHub. Anyone can browse, clone (git clone https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum) and read the full history, tags and releases without an account.
repo_track_justification: The repository uses Git (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum), which records for every commit what changed (the full diff), who made it (author and committer), and when (timestamps). Commit messages follow a `type: description` convention, AI-assisted commits carry a Co-Authored-By trailer, and history is browsable at https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/commits/main.
repo_interim_justification: All development happens in the public repository: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum has 1,276 commits on main against 65 tagged releases, so interim work is visible between every release. Each change lands as individual feat/fix/test/docs commits on a branch, merged into main with a merge commit, before the release commit that tags it — e.g. v5.12.0..v5.13.0 contains the feature commit 3d83d91 separate from the release commit 6eff45f. Full history: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: The source repository uses Git, a common distributed version control system: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique semantic version number (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, e.g. 5.20.0), set in package.json and wrangler.toml, tagged in Git (v5.20.0) and published as a GitHub Release (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/releases). The running site reports its exact version and Git commit ID at https://wempos-forum.com/api/version (e.g. {"version":"5.20.0","commit":"549661c"}).
version_semver_justification: The project uses Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (declared in CHANGELOG.md; versions are MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, e.g. 5.20.0). A Versioning section defining the public API (/api/* routes, MCP tools, self-hosting config, migrations) is in CONTRIBUTING.md (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#versioning).
version_tags_justification: Every release is tagged vX.Y.Z in git (e.g. v5.19.0, v5.20.0) with a matching GitHub Release.
release_notes_justification:
URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

Every release has an entry in CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog format, newest first): a plain-language summary of what changed for members and admins — new features, privacy and security fixes, and behavior changes — rather than raw commit logs. Entries are drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code) and reviewed by the maintainer. Each release also has a git tag and a GitHub Release with notes at https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/releases.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability (CVE, GHSA or similar) has ever been assigned to this project — the repository has zero published security advisories. Security fixes found by the project's own reviews are described in plain language in CHANGELOG.md, and any future advisory with a CVE will be listed in the release notes of the version that fixes it.
report_process_justification: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/issues/new/choose — bugs are reported through GitHub Issues using the bug-report form (bug_report.yml), with a separate feature-request form. Forum members can also post in the "Bugs & Troubleshooting & Help" board at https://wempos-forum.com. Security problems are reported privately instead, as described in SECURITY.md.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/issues) tracks each bug and feature request on its own, with bug-report and feature-request forms, labels (bug, enhancement, accessibility, i18n, good first issue, and more), and links to the commits that close them.
report_responses_justification: The repository is new (created 2026-10-10), so the 2-12 month window is still short; every issue filed so far has been acknowledged and resolved — 4 of 4 issues closed, including both bug reports (#3 syntax error, closed within a day; #17 production failure, fixed and closed). So far reports have come from the maintainer; new reports from anyone are handled through the GitHub issue forms. https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: Every enhancement request so far has been answered and implemented: #41 (proper translations — discussed and shipped, the forum now has 41 languages) and #44 (documentation rewrite with CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG and SECURITY — shipped and closed the same day). The repository is new (created 2026-10-10), so the window is short and requests so far have come from the maintainer; new requests from anyone go through the feature-request form. https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement
report_archive_justification: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/issues?q=is%3Aissue — GitHub Issues keeps every report and every response permanently, including closed ones, publicly readable and searchable without an account; each issue and comment has its own URL. Forum members' reports in the public "Bugs & Troubleshooting & Help" board at https://wempos-forum.com are likewise kept and searchable.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/SECURITY.md — the security policy explains how to report vulnerabilities privately: GitHub private vulnerability reporting (enabled: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/security/advisories/new) or email to the maintainer, and asks reporters not to open public issues for security problems. GitHub also links it from the repository's Security tab.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled on GitHub (Security tab → "Report a vulnerability", https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/security/advisories/new), and SECURITY.md also offers a private email address. Only the maintainers can see reports.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received so far (0 security advisories), so none have gone unanswered. Reports go to the maintainer through GitHub private reporting or email per SECURITY.md. (Optional, owner's choice: add "You'll get a first reply within 14 days" to SECURITY.md.)
build_justification: The forum is plain JavaScript (ES modules) with no compile step; Cloudflare's wrangler acts as the build system, automatically bundling the worker from source on every run. After changing the source, `pnpm run dev` rebuilds and runs it locally and `pnpm run deploy` rebuilds and deploys it (`pnpm exec wrangler deploy --dry-run` shows the build output). Browser files in public/ are served as-is. Self-hosters build and deploy their own instance the same way, following docs/self-hosting.md with wrangler.example.toml. See https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum#running-it-locally and https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md
build_common_tools_justification: The build uses standard, widely used tools: pnpm (package manager and script runner, scripts defined in package.json), Cloudflare's wrangler (which bundles the worker with esbuild), and Node.js's built-in test runner (node --test). No custom build tooling.
build_floss_tools_justification: Everything needed to build, run and test it locally is free software: Node.js (MIT), pnpm (MIT), Cloudflare's wrangler (MIT/Apache-2.0) with esbuild (MIT), and the workerd runtime used by `wrangler dev` (Apache-2.0). Deploying to Cloudflare's hosted platform is an optional hosting choice, not part of the build.
test_justification: The project ships an automated test suite in the public repository under the same AGPLv3-or-later license (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/tree/main/tests): about 1,013 tests run with Node.js's built-in test runner, driving the real worker handlers against an in-memory SQLite D1 and a fake DOM. How to run it is documented in README.md ("Running the tests": `pnpm install` then `pnpm test`) and CONTRIBUTING.md, and CI runs it on every push to main and every pull request (.github/workflows/test.yml).
test_invocation_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/package.json — The tests run with the standard Node.js command `pnpm test` (the equivalent of `npm test`), the "test" script in package.json, which runs Node's built-in test runner (`node --test`). This is documented in README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.
test_most_justification: The automated suite (about 1,013 tests, run with `pnpm test`) covers most of the code: 82% of branches, 79% of functions and 77% of lines, measured with Node's built-in coverage (`node --test --experimental-test-coverage`) on 2026-11-21. Route input validation and every visibility/permission rule have dedicated tests, including cross-route privacy sweeps, and new features land with tests written to fail first.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/actions/workflows/test.yml — Changes are merged into main many times a day (65+ releases since October 2026). Every push to main and every pull request runs the full automated suite (`pnpm test`, about 1,188 tests) and ESLint in GitHub Actions, with CodeQL, Semgrep, ShellCheck, Gitleaks, REUSE and a pnpm audit running beside them.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#making-a-change) requires every change to add or update tests ("Bug fixes should come with a test that fails without the fix") and `pnpm test` to pass before a pull request. In practice every new feature lands with tests written to fail first (e.g. each 2026-11 release adds its own tests/wave*.test.mjs file).
tests_are_added_justification: Every recent release that added functionality added tests for it in the same change: v5.13.0 poll close/take-back → tests/wave513-polls.test.mjs (12 tests); v5.14.0 backup-codes/sign-out-other-devices → tests/wave514-account-security.test.mjs (16); v5.15.0 staff-only Polls board → tests/staff-only-boards.test.mjs (6); v5.17.0 self-hosting → tests/self-hosting.test.mjs (16). The suite grew from 769 tests at v5.3.0 to 953 at v5.17.0 on 2026-11-21. Release notes: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
tests_documented_added_justification: The change-proposal instructions in CONTRIBUTING.md, "Making a change" (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#making-a-change), say step 3: "Add or update tests. Bug fixes should come with a test that fails without the fix", and step 4: run `pnpm test`. The Code review section repeats the requirement.
warnings_justification: All code is written as JavaScript ES modules (worker.mjs, api/*.mjs, public/js/*.js loaded as type="module"), which always run in JavaScript's strict mode — the "use strict" safe language mode — automatically. In addition, ESLint (MIT, recommended rules, `pnpm lint`) runs in CI on every push to main and every pull request, and ShellCheck checks every shell script; GitHub CodeQL and Semgrep CE scan for code-quality and security mistakes on every push, with 0 open code-scanning alerts (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/security/code-scanning).
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are fixed as they appear: ESLint's findings were fixed or justified in the code when it was introduced and lint must pass in CI; all code-scanning (CodeQL) alerts have been resolved — 11 on 2026-11-21 (commit c9e3bba) and 5 more later the same day — leaving 0 open alerts: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/security/code-scanning
warnings_strict_justification: All code runs in JavaScript strict mode, because every file is an ES module. ESLint's recommended rules run in CI on every push and pull request and must pass, ShellCheck checks every shell script, and every GitHub CodeQL and Semgrep alert is fixed as it appears, including alerts in test files that never ship (16 CodeQL alerts fixed on 2026-11-21 alone, 0 open).
know_secure_design_justification: The primary developer (the project's founder and maintainer, who receives private vulnerability reports and performs all releases) knows and applies secure-design principles, visible throughout the code: fail-safe defaults and complete mediation (every write goes through requireUser → CSRF + same-origin checks; every read that returns posts or members goes through one shared visibility law that denies hidden, banned and block-paired content by default — api/core/visibility.mjs); least privilege and limited attack surface (staff-only actions gated server-side, not just hidden in the UI; staff-only boards in one allowlist; new features like AutoMod ship disabled by default); separation of privilege (two-factor sign-in with backup codes); open design (security rests on secrets like the password pepper and session tokens, stored hashed, not on obscurity); input validation with allowlists (usernames must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,24}$, boards/roles come from fixed allowlists); economy of mechanism (no framework, no bundler, plain modules); and psychological acceptability (privacy features opt-in and plainly explained). See docs/architecture.md and SECURITY.md.
know_common_errors_justification: The primary developer knows the common web-application vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10 / CWE Top 25) and the project applies a mitigation for each: SQL injection — every D1 query uses bound parameters (prepare().bind()), with fragments built only from constants; cross-site scripting — user text is rendered with textContent, never innerHTML, under a strict Content-Security-Policy; CSRF — every state-changing request requires a same-origin check plus an X-CSRF-Token tied to the session; broken authentication — passwords hashed with a server-side pepper, session tokens stored only as hashes, optional TOTP two-factor, rate-limited sign-in, Turnstile; broken access control / missing authorization — all staff-only actions and boards enforced server-side, one shared visibility law for hidden/banned/blocked content, and cross-route privacy test sweeps; open redirect — canonical redirects only to a configured origin; sensitive-data exposure — secrets never in responses, logs or the repo. GitHub CodeQL scans every push (all alerts fixed) and security reviews run every few releases (see CHANGELOG.md).
crypto_published_justification: All cryptography uses publicly published, expert-reviewed standard algorithms via the platform's Web Crypto API (crypto.subtle) — no home-made crypto: passwords are hashed with PBKDF2 (HMAC-SHA-256) plus a server-side pepper (HMAC-SHA-256) (api/core/passwords.mjs); session tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and generated with crypto.getRandomValues (api/core/crypto.mjs, api/core/auth.mjs); signed values use HMAC-SHA-256; two-factor codes follow the TOTP standard (RFC 6238); all traffic uses TLS 1.3. No MD5 or Math.random is used for security.
crypto_call_justification: The forum does not implement any cryptographic primitives itself. All hashing, key derivation, HMAC and random generation call the platform's Web Crypto API (crypto.subtle and crypto.getRandomValues), which is purpose-built cryptographic software provided by the Cloudflare Workers runtime: PBKDF2 and HMAC-SHA-256 for passwords, SHA-256 for session-token hashes, HMAC for signed values. The two-factor (TOTP, RFC 6238) code only does the standard's counter/truncation steps around an HMAC computed by crypto.subtle. TLS is handled entirely by Cloudflare's servers that host the forum.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography the forum depends on is implementable with free software: PBKDF2, HMAC-SHA-256 and SHA-256 via the standard Web Crypto API (implemented in the free workerd/V8 runtime and every FLOSS browser/Node.js), TOTP per the public RFC 6238 (works with any free authenticator app), and TLS 1.3 (free implementations such as OpenSSL/BoringSSL). No proprietary or patented-only algorithm is required; a self-hosted copy runs entirely on free software (workerd + wrangler, Apache-2.0/MIT).
crypto_keylength_justification: Default key and hash lengths meet or exceed the NIST 2030 minimums: session tokens are 256-bit random values (crypto.getRandomValues, randomToken(32)) and CSRF tokens 192-bit; stored token hashes and HMACs use SHA-256 (256-bit); passwords use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with a server-side pepper. Transport is TLS 1.3, where the minimum TLS version is configurable in Cloudflare so older protocols and short keys can be fully disabled. Two-factor codes use HMAC-SHA-1 with a 160-bit secret only because the TOTP standard (RFC 6238) and authenticator apps require it for interoperability; NIST still approves HMAC-SHA-1 for message authentication, since HMAC's strength doesn't rely on SHA-1's collision resistance.
crypto_working_justification: Complete inventory of cryptography in the code (2026-11-21): SHA-256 (token/key hashing), HMAC-SHA-256 (signing, password pepper), PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 (password hashing), HMAC-SHA-1 (TOTP two-factor only), and the system CSPRNG (crypto.getRandomValues / randomUUID) — all via the Web Crypto API. The forum performs no encryption itself (so no block-cipher modes are used); transport is TLS 1.3 with AEAD ciphers. HMAC-SHA-1 is used only because the TOTP standard (RFC 6238) and authenticator apps require it; it remains secure for message authentication since HMAC does not rely on SHA-1's collision resistance. Math.random appears only for non-security HTML element ids.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No default security mechanism relies on an algorithm or mode with known serious weaknesses. Token hashing, signing and password hashing use SHA-256 (HMAC-SHA-256, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256), and transport is TLS 1.3 with no CBC. The only SHA-1 use is HMAC-SHA-1 inside TOTP two-factor codes, which RFC 6238 requires for authenticator-app compatibility. HMAC doesn't depend on collision resistance, which is the property SHA-1 has lost.
crypto_pfs_justification: The forum implements no key-agreement protocol of its own. Every connection uses HTTPS with TLS 1.3, handled by Cloudflare's servers that host the forum, and TLS 1.3 always provides perfect forward secrecy through ephemeral (EC)DHE key exchange — so a later compromise of a long-term key cannot decrypt past sessions.
crypto_password_storage_justification:
Passwords are never stored in plaintext. Each is hashed with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 using a unique 16-byte random salt per user (crypto.getRandomValues) and 100,000 iterations — the maximum the Cloudflare Workers Web Crypto API permits — after a pre-hashing pepper (HMAC-SHA-256 keyed by a server-side secret stored outside the database, per OWASP's peppering guidance). Verification uses a constant-time comparison. See api/core/passwords.mjs and constants.mjs (PBKDF2_ITERATIONS).
(Known gap, stated honestly: OWASP now recommends 600,000 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 iterations; the forum uses 100,000 because that is the Workers Web Crypto cap. Moving to Argon2id is an owner decision because of per-sign-in CPU cost.)
crypto_random_justification:
Every cryptographic key, token, salt and nonce is generated with the platform CSPRNG, crypto.getRandomValues (Web Crypto), directly or through the shared randomToken() helper (api/core/crypto.mjs:49-50): session tokens (randomToken(32), 256-bit) and CSRF tokens (randomToken(24)) in api/core/auth.mjs; two-factor TOTP secrets (20 random bytes, api/core/totp.mjs:75); backup codes (randomToken(6), api/twofa.mjs:210); password salts (16 random bytes, api/core/passwords.mjs:98); IDs via crypto.randomUUID. Math.random is never used for security — its only use is generating unique HTML element ids on a staff form (public/js/desk/bans.js).
Short version: All keys, tokens, salts and nonces come from the Web Crypto CSPRNG (crypto.getRandomValues / crypto.randomUUID): 256-bit session tokens, CSRF tokens, 160-bit TOTP secrets, backup codes and per-user password salts (api/core/crypto.mjs, totp.mjs, passwords.mjs). Math.random is used only for non-security HTML element ids.
delivery_mitm_justification: The software is delivered only over HTTPS: the source and tagged releases come from GitHub (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum, cloned over HTTPS or SSH), and the running forum is served at https://wempos-forum.com with TLS 1.3 and HSTS (HTTP redirects to HTTPS). Dependencies are installed by pnpm over HTTPS from the npm registry, pinned and integrity-checked by the committed lockfile (pnpm-lock.yaml); CI actions are pinned to full commit SHAs.
delivery_unsigned_justification: The project never retrieves a cryptographic hash over plain HTTP and trusts it without a signature check. The forum is delivered only over HTTPS (TLS 1.3) from https://wempos-forum.com and the source over HTTPS from GitHub. In CI, dependencies come from the npm registry over HTTPS and are verified against the integrity hashes committed in pnpm-lock.yaml (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`); the one downloaded binary (Gitleaks) is fetched over HTTPS and checked against a SHA-256 value committed in the workflow file, not fetched at run time; all GitHub Actions are pinned by full commit SHA. No http:// download appears anywhere in CI or scripts.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no unpatched vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity, publicly known or otherwise: GitHub shows 0 open Dependabot alerts, 0 open code-scanning (CodeQL) alerts and 0 open secret-scanning alerts; `pnpm audit --prod` reports no known vulnerabilities; and there are 0 security advisories. Dependencies are audited on every push and weekly.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerabilities have been reported or found. The project ships several releases a day with a tested deploy pipeline, so a critical fix can be released within hours of being confirmed; reports go through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or the email in SECURITY.md.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The public repository does not leak any valid private credential. Secrets (the password pepper, API keys, tokens) are stored only as Cloudflare Worker secrets, never in the repo; .dev.vars, .env and .env.* are git-ignored and have never been committed in any branch's history. Gitleaks scans the full git history on every push (clean; the only matches are three public test-fixture values that are allowlisted by exact value), and GitHub secret scanning reports 0 alerts (open or resolved).
static_analysis_justification: At least one static analysis tool runs on every push to main and every pull request, before any release: GitHub CodeQL (default setup; its engine is proprietary but free for public repositories), Semgrep Community Edition (LGPL-2.1, free software; javascript, nodejs and secrets rule packs), ESLint (MIT; recommended rules, `pnpm lint`), ShellCheck (GPL-3.0; every tracked shell script) and Gitleaks (MIT; full git history scanned for leaked secrets). All run in GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/) and must pass before a deploy. See docs/security-tooling.md. Pull requests additionally get Codacy (static code analysis), Aikido Security (code, dependency and secret checks) and AI code review from CodeRabbit and Sourcery; these are third-party services that run on pull requests only, while the tools above run on every push to main.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: Semgrep Community Edition (LGPL-2.1, free software; javascript, nodejs and secrets rule packs) runs on every push and pull request and looks specifically for common vulnerabilities, alongside GitHub CodeQL's JavaScript security queries (XSS, injection, ReDoS, incomplete sanitization) and Gitleaks for committed secrets.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Every medium-or-higher static analysis finding has been fixed: GitHub shows 0 open code-scanning alerts (earlier CodeQL alerts — e.g. ReDoS, incomplete multi-character sanitization, URL substring checks, a TOCTOU race, unpinned actions — were all fixed and closed). Deploys wait for CodeQL to report 0 open alerts on the pushed commit.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every push to main and every pull request (CodeQL, Semgrep, ESLint, ShellCheck, Gitleaks), so it runs many times a day.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Dynamic analysis runs on every candidate before release. The automated suite (about 1,188 tests on node:test) runs the real request handlers, including fast-check property-based fuzz tests that throw thousands of random and malformed inputs at sign-in, search, posting and the validators. It runs on every push and must pass before deploy. OWASP ZAP baseline (Apache-2.0) also runs a passive scan every week and on demand against a copy of the forum started inside CI (.github/workflows/zap-baseline.yml; docs/security-tooling.md).
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The forum is written entirely in JavaScript, a memory-safe language, and has no C/C++ or other memory-unsafe code, so memory-safety tools such as ASan, MSan or UBSan don't apply.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The software checks its invariants at run time and fails closed: requireUser and assertSameOrigin throw on a missing session, CSRF token or origin; validators reject out-of-range input; password hashing refuses to run without a valid pepper; malformed stored credentials verify as false. The dynamic tests run with node:assert/strict assertions on every run, and any failure fails CI and blocks deploys.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No medium-or-higher exploitable vulnerability has been found by dynamic analysis. The ZAP baseline scan of the forum (2026-11-21, run 44962197840) reported one Medium alert, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on five public, read-only discovery files (/.well-known/api-catalog, /auth.md, /openapi.json, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml); this is intentional so agents can read them, credentials are never allowed cross-origin (no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials anywhere), and the sitemap lists only public pages, so it is not exploitable. Everything else was Low or informational. The fuzz tests have never produced a crash or a server error. Any confirmed medium-or-higher finding would be fixed in the next release.
achieve_passing_justification: The project earned the passing badge (100%) for project 16994: https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/16994
dco_justification: There is no DCO, CLA or other legal mechanism for contributors to state that they have the right to contribute. Commits aren't required to carry Signed-off-by, and CONTRIBUTING.md doesn't ask for it. Inbound code is accepted under the project license (AGPLv3-or-later, per CONTRIBUTING.md "License headers"), but nobody explicitly asserts their authority to contribute. To meet this, CONTRIBUTING.md would have to require `git commit -s` and a DCO check would have to run in CI.
governance_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-decisions-are-made — The project documents a single-maintainer governance model. The maintainer (ItsWempo) makes the final decision on what is merged, released and planned. Anyone can take part through issues, pull requests, Discussions or the forum's Suggestions board. Disagreements are raised on the issue or pull request, the maintainer answers with reasoning, and decisions can be reopened with new information. Project-wide rules are recorded in CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md.
code_of_conduct_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md — The project adopts the Contributor Covenant 3.0 and keeps it in the standard location (CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md at the repository root, linked from the README and from GitHub's community profile). It covers encouraged and restricted behaviors, how to report an issue, and how harm is addressed.
roles_responsibilities_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities — GOVERNANCE.md lists the key roles and who holds each one. Maintainer (ItsWempo, who is also owner, release manager and security contact): direction, review and merge, releases (version bump, CHANGELOG, signed tag, GitHub Release, deploy), migrations, deploy credentials and secrets, issue triage, vulnerability handling, Code of Conduct enforcement. Contributor: anyone, following CONTRIBUTING.md. Forum staff: community moderators on the hosted site, with no rights over code or releases. It states plainly that the maintainer currently does every maintainer task, and that AI agents and review bots are not project members.
access_continuity_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity-and-bus-factor — The project can't yet keep going within a week of losing its one maintainer. The code, history, signed tags and releases are public under AGPLv3, and the release, deploy and self-hosting steps are documented (docs/release-checklist.md, docs/self-hosting.md), so anyone could fork it. But no second person has documented authority to create and close issues, accept changes and cut releases, and the hosting credentials and owner-held secrets (such as the password pepper) are held only by the maintainer. GOVERNANCE.md describes this gap and the fix: a second trusted maintainer with org owner rights and a sealed credential hand-over. That fix is on the roadmap.
bus_factor_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity-and-bus-factor — The bus factor is 1. All human commits come from one person, ItsWempo. The other commits come from bots (Dependabot, DeepSource autofix, Qodana) and from AI-assisted work (Co-Authored-By: Claude Code). Losing that one person would stop development and releases. GOVERNANCE.md says so openly, and ROADMAP.md lists recruiting a second maintainer as a goal.
documentation_roadmap_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/ROADMAP.md — ROADMAP.md covers November 2026 to November 2027. Goals: keep the forum secure and private, make self-hosting easier, move images from D1 to R2, improve translations and accessibility, reduce the bus factor, raise statement coverage above 90%, and respond to community requests. Non-goals: no ads, trackers or data sales; no browser framework or bundler; no storage beyond D1/R2; no WebRTC voice or video; no third-party bot marketplace; no support for old versions.
documentation_architecture_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/architecture.md — docs/architecture.md describes the high-level design. It covers the Cloudflare Worker entry point (worker.mjs) and its rate limiting and routing; the feature modules in api/, grouped by area; the shared core in api/core/ (sessions and CSRF, roles, the visibility rule, errors, password hashing, TOTP, image checks); sign-in through the separate Wempo Accounts worker over a private service binding; the browser app in public/ (plain ES modules, no build step); D1 data and numbered migrations; the tests; and deploys. Trust boundaries are drawn in docs/assurance-case.md.
documentation_security_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/security-requirements.md — The page lists, in plain language, what users can expect: salted, peppered PBKDF2 password storage; hashed 256-bit session tokens in __Host- Secure HttpOnly cookies; TOTP two-factor; rate limits; HTTPS with HSTS; CSRF and same-origin checks on every write; strict CSP; the visibility rule for hidden, banned and blocked content; byte-sniffed uploads; data export and account deletion; and signed releases. It also lists what users can't expect: privacy from the operator (DMs are not end-to-end encrypted), permanent deletion on demand, anonymity, protection from compromised devices, security of modified self-hosted copies, old-version support, or a guaranteed fix time.
documentation_quick_start_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum#running-it-locally — The README's "Running it locally" section gets a new user running in a few commands: git clone, pnpm install, pnpm run db:migrate:local, pnpm run dev, then open the local site. Members can start straight away at https://wempos-forum.com with the guide in docs/using-the-forum.md, and docs/self-hosting.md is a numbered quick path to running your own instance.
documentation_current_justification: The docs are updated in the same change as the behavior they describe: CONTRIBUTING.md's review checklist requires updating docs, translations and CHANGELOG.md when behavior changes. Every release adds a CHANGELOG.md entry. The README, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/api.md and docs/self-hosting.md were rewritten in issue #44 and have been kept current since. Known doc defects are fixed as they're found, for example the 2026-11-21 commits that corrected the badge answers and the release-checklist steps.
documentation_achievements_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum#readme — The README (the repository front page) shows the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, linked to https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/16994, next to the CI badge.
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The web interface follows WCAG practices where reasonable. It uses semantic HTML with ARIA roles, labels and live regions (around 50 browser modules use aria- attributes); everything works from the keyboard, with managed focus (for example, focus moves to the page heading on navigation so screen-reader and keyboard users keep their place, per docs/moderation.md); there is a high-contrast mode, adjustable reading comfort and prefers-reduced-motion support (styles.css); and images get translated alt text. tests/a11y-wave7.test.mjs checks accessibility behavior, and GitHub issues use an "accessibility" label. No formal WCAG audit has been done yet.
internationalization_justification: The interface is internationalized: every user-facing string is looked up by key from per-language JSON catalogs in public/locales/ (41 languages today), with English as the fallback. Users pick a language in settings, and community translation is hooked up through Crowdin (issue #41, PR #42). Locale tests check that every catalog has the expected shape.
sites_password_security_justification: Wempo's Forum (https://wempos-forum.com, with sign-in at https://accounts.wempos-forum.com) stores user passwords only as salted, iterated hashes: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with 100,000 iterations and a unique 16-byte random salt per user, after an HMAC-SHA-256 pepper keyed by a secret kept outside the database (api/core/passwords.mjs). The repository host, GitHub, meets this criterion itself.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported (SECURITY.md "Supported Versions"), and there's a simple upgrade path from any older version. docs/self-hosting.md "Updating later" (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md#updating-later) says: git pull, pnpm install, apply the database migrations, pnpm run deploy. Database changes ship as additive numbered migrations that are never edited after release, so they apply in order from any older version. Behavior changes and upgrade notes are written up in CHANGELOG.md, and breaking changes follow SemVer (CONTRIBUTING.md "Versioning").
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability reports have come from outside reporters in the last 12 months. The repository has 0 security advisories, and every security fix in that time came from the project's own reviews (docs/security-reviews/). SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters by name or handle unless they ask to stay anonymous.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-we-respond-to-a-report — SECURITY.md documents the response process: acknowledge (normally within 14 days); triage and rate severity; fix privately in a GitHub security advisory or private branch, with a regression test; release a signed fix and deploy it (critical as fast as possible, medium or worse within 60 days); publish an advisory (with a CVE where warranted) and a CHANGELOG entry, crediting the reporter; then look for the same mistake elsewhere and update the assurance case.
coding_standards_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-standards — The JavaScript style guide is ESLint's recommended rule set (@eslint/js configs.recommended), configured in eslint.config.js (ECMAScript 2023 modules, globals per runtime). The project's differences and additions are listed: plain ES modules with no framework or bundler, textContent only, the shared visibility helpers, the api() wrapper, ShellCheck for shell scripts, and the license header. Contributions follow it: `pnpm lint` passes on main.
coding_standards_enforced_justification: The style guide is enforced automatically. ESLint (`pnpm lint`) runs in GitHub Actions on every push and pull request (.github/workflows/test.yml), along with ShellCheck (shellcheck.yml), `reuse lint` (reuse.yml) and the license-header test inside `pnpm test`. Exceptions are rare: only vendored files and docs/ are excluded, in eslint.config.js's ignores list.
build_standard_variables_justification: There's no native (C/C++) build. The project is plain JavaScript; the only build step is Wrangler bundling the worker with esbuild, and the browser files ship unchanged. CC, CFLAGS, CXX, CXXFLAGS and LDFLAGS don't apply.
build_preserve_debug_justification: No native binaries are built or stripped. The browser runs the original JavaScript source unchanged, and the worker bundle is unminified esbuild output with a source map (worker.js.map), so all debugging information is kept.
build_non_recursive_justification: The build isn't recursive. One Wrangler/esbuild invocation bundles the whole worker from worker.mjs and its imports, and public/ is served as-is. There are no sub-directory builds.
build_repeatable_justification: The build is bit-for-bit repeatable. Two `wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir` builds of the same commit (d84e01f, v5.30.0, run 2026-11-22) produced a byte-identical worker.js. The only differences were the output folder recorded in worker.js.map's sourceRoot and a timestamp in Wrangler's generated README, and neither is part of the deployed code. Toolchain versions are pinned in pnpm-lock.yaml. Steps: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/release-checklist.md#reproducing-the-build
installation_common_justification: Installation uses the usual conventions for its platform: dependencies via pnpm (`pnpm install`), the database via `wrangler d1 migrations apply`, and the forum itself via `pnpm run deploy` (wrangler deploy) to a Cloudflare Worker, as docs/self-hosting.md (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md) describes. To uninstall, run `wrangler delete` and `wrangler d1 delete`, or for local development just delete the clone.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Nothing is installed into the local filesystem hierarchy (/usr, /opt, etc.). The software deploys as a Cloudflare Worker, or runs from its own checkout under `wrangler dev`, so DESTDIR, prefix and similar location variables don't apply. Local state lives in the project's .wrangler/ folder.
installation_development_quick_justifica: Developers get everything — the code, the dev environment and the tests — with the usual pnpm steps: git clone, pnpm install, pnpm run db:migrate:local, pnpm run dev, pnpm test (README "Running it locally" and "Running the tests", CONTRIBUTING.md "Setting up": https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#setting-up). All tools, including Wrangler and the local workerd runtime, come from the lockfile. No external services are needed: tests run against an in-memory SQLite D1.
external_dependencies_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/package.json — External dependencies are listed in machine-readable form in package.json and pinned with integrity hashes in pnpm-lock.yaml (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/pnpm-lock.yaml). There are no runtime npm dependencies; the dev dependencies are eslint, @eslint/js, globals, fast-check and wrangler.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependencies are checked for known vulnerabilities automatically. `pnpm audit` runs on every push, every pull request and weekly (.github/workflows/audit.yml, Mondays 06:17 UTC). GitHub Dependabot alerts are on, and Dependabot opens update PRs (e.g. #33, undici). There are currently 0 open alerts and `pnpm audit` reports no known vulnerabilities. There are no convenience copies of third-party code.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: All reused third-party components come through pnpm, so they're easy to find (package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml) and update (`pnpm update`, Dependabot PRs). The project contains no forked or copied third-party code: api/vendor/ holds two of the project's own modules, kept byte-for-byte on purpose (see REUSE.toml), not upstream copies.
interfaces_current_justification: The project uses current, non-deprecated interfaces: ES modules everywhere, fetch() (not XMLHttpRequest) through one api() wrapper, the standard Web Crypto API, Cloudflare D1's prepare().bind() API, ESLint flat config, and Node's built-in test runner. ESLint and CodeQL flag deprecated usage in CI.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: Every push to main and every pull request runs the full automated suite (about 1,188 tests via `pnpm test`, driving the real request handlers against an in-memory D1) plus ESLint in GitHub Actions, and reports pass or fail on the commit: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/actions/workflows/test.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: More than half of recent bug fixes came with regression tests. Of the 99 non-merge `fix:` commits from 2026-05-21 to 2026-11-21 (the repository was created 2026-10-10), 58 (59%) changed or added files under tests/ in the same commit, and more fixes got their test in a companion commit in the same release. CONTRIBUTING.md requires bug fixes to come with a test that fails without the fix.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Statement coverage is about 89%: 88.71% of lines, 88.86% of branches and 90.80% of functions, measured with Node's built-in free coverage tool (`node --test --experimental-test-coverage`) on origin/main at d84e01f (v5.30.0) on 2026-11-22, with 1,188 tests and 0 failures. (Node reports line coverage, which here stands in for statement coverage.)
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md is the written policy: new functionality and bug fixes must come with tests in the automated suite ("Add or update tests. Bug fixes should come with a test that fails without the fix"), and the code review checklist won't accept a change without tests (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-review). In practice every feature release adds its own test files.
implement_secure_design_justification: Secure-design principles are built into the code, with the argument in https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md#3-secure-design-principles-saltzer-and-schroeder. Fail-safe defaults: routes deny unless checks pass, and malformed sessions or hashes fail closed. Complete mediation: every write goes through requireUser (session, CSRF and same-origin checks), and every content read goes through the shared visibility helpers, with cross-route tests. Economy of mechanism: small shared api/core/ modules and no runtime dependencies. Open design. Least privilege: moderator-only powers, the Accounts worker can't read password hashes, CI runs with contents: read. Separation of privilege: TOTP two-factor.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The algorithms are fixed in code. Password records store only a salt and a hash, with no algorithm or iteration identifier (api/core/passwords.mjs, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 at the PBKDF2_ITERATIONS constant), and token hashing is fixed to SHA-256. Switching algorithms would take a code change, plus rehashing passwords at login or forcing resets. Users can't pick another algorithm. Storing a versioned hash format would meet this.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: Credentials and keys are kept apart from the code, configuration files, database and logs. The password pepper, setup secret, relay token, Turnstile secret and other keys are Cloudflare Worker secrets, set through stdin with `wrangler secret put` and never committed (.dev.vars is git-ignored; Gitleaks scans history). They can be changed without rebuilding or changing code. One caveat: rotating the pepper makes existing password hashes unverifiable, so it would need a reset or rehash.
crypto_used_network_justification: All network traffic uses secure protocols. The forum and Accounts sites are HTTPS only (TLS 1.3; HTTP gets a 301 to HTTPS; HSTS max-age=31536000). The worker's only outbound internet request is HTTPS to Cloudflare Turnstile's siteverify endpoint, and forum-to-Accounts traffic goes over a private Cloudflare service binding. Source and releases come from GitHub over HTTPS or SSH. No insecure protocol (HTTP, FTP, telnet, SSLv3) is used or enabled.
crypto_tls12_justification: TLS 1.2 and newer are supported. https://wempos-forum.com and https://accounts.wempos-forum.com negotiate TLS 1.3 through Cloudflare's edge, which also supports TLS 1.2. SSL and other obsolete protocols aren't offered.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Certificate verification is on by default everywhere. The worker's outbound HTTPS call (Turnstile) uses the Workers runtime's fetch(), which always verifies TLS certificates, and nothing in the code turns that off. Browsers verify the site's certificates, including for subresources, all of which are same-origin or HTTPS.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Private data is only ever sent after the certificate is verified. The session cookie is __Host-wempo_session with Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax (api/core/auth.mjs), so browsers only send it over verified HTTPS, and HSTS makes sure browsers never try plain HTTP. The Turnstile secret goes only over the runtime's verified HTTPS fetch.
signed_releases_justification: Releases are signed. Every release since v4.5.0 is a GPG-signed annotated tag vX.Y.Z (Ed25519 key 1A72F3E35BD7E5D014B7B8555A7455E71384675E, verified with `git tag -v`), with a matching GitHub Release. SECURITY.md "Verifying a release" (https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release) explains how to get the public key (https://github.com/ItsWempo.gpg) and verify a tag. Signing happens on the maintainer's machine; GitHub and the host hold only the public key.
version_tags_signed_justification: All version tags since v4.5.0, including every release from v5.0.0 to v5.30.0, are GPG-signed annotated tags, and `git tag -v v5.30.0` reports a good signature from the maintainer's key (fingerprint 1A72 F3E3 5BD7 E5D0 14B7 B855 5A74 55E7 1384 675E).
input_validation_justification: All untrusted input is checked against allow-lists at the route boundary. Examples: passwords must be strings of 12–128 characters; stored salts and hashes must be fixed-length hex; IDs, enums, lengths and formats are checked in each handler; JSON bodies are capped at 16 KB (MAX_JSON_BYTES); uploads are accepted by sniffing their bytes against a list of allowed image types (api/core/images.mjs). Invalid input gets a 4xx error. fast-check fuzz tests throw thousands of malformed inputs at sign-in, search, posting and the validators.
hardening_justification: Hardening is used so that defects are less likely to become vulnerabilities. Every response, including static assets (run_worker_first = true), carries a strict Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self', no inline script, object-src 'none', frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and Cross-Origin-Opener/Resource-Policy: same-origin (api/vendor/http.mjs). Cookies use the __Host- prefix with Secure and HttpOnly. Uploads are served with nosniff and a fixed type. See https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
assurance_case_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md — The assurance case gives: a threat model (assets; attackers from anonymous visitors to supply-chain and network attackers; what's out of scope); the trust boundaries (browser to worker, worker to D1, forum to the Accounts service binding, worker to Turnstile, repository to CI/deploy); an argument for each Saltzer and Schroeder secure-design principle; and a table showing how each OWASP Top 10 2021 category and the relevant CWE Top 25 weaknesses are countered, with the code and tests as evidence.
achieve_silver_justification: Silver isn't earned yet. The silver MUST criterion access_continuity is Unmet: the hosting credentials and maintainer rights rest with one person. Silver's SHOULD criteria dco, bus_factor and crypto_algorithm_agility are Unmet too.
contributors_unassociated_justification: There aren't two unassociated significant contributors. All significant human contributions in the past year come from one person, the maintainer ItsWempo. The other commits are from bots (Dependabot, DeepSource autofix, Qodana) or are AI-assisted work directed by the maintainer. Contributors: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/graphs/contributors
copyright_per_file_justification: Not every source file has a copyright statement of its own. Every .js, .mjs and .css file starts with "Copyright 2026 ItsWempo" and SPDX-FileCopyrightText (enforced by tests/license-headers.test.mjs). But the 55 SQL migrations (49 have no header), the 3 shell scripts and public/index.html get their copyright only from REUSE.toml, not from a line in the file. Released migrations are never edited, so adding headers to them would mean changing that rule.
license_per_file_justification: Not every source file has a license statement of its own. Every .js, .mjs and .css file carries the AGPLv3-or-later notice and SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later (enforced by tests/license-headers.test.mjs; `reuse lint` passes). But the SQL migrations, the shell scripts and public/index.html are licensed only through REUSE.toml, with no line in the file itself.
small_tasks_justification: The repository has "good first issue" and "help wanted" labels and labels for time-to-complete, but there are currently no open issues marked as small tasks for newcomers. The only one so far (#41) is closed. Labels: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/labels
require_2FA_justification: The project doesn't require two-factor authentication. The Wempo-s-Silly-Projects GitHub organization has "Require two-factor authentication" turned off (two_factor_requirement_enabled: false, checked 2026-11-22). To meet this, the owner would turn that setting on.
secure_2FA_justification: Since the project doesn't require 2FA (see require_2FA), it can't guarantee that developers use a cryptographic method (TOTP, a security key or a passkey) rather than SMS. Meeting this means requiring org 2FA and confirming that every member uses TOTP, a passkey or a security key.
code_review_standards_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-review — CONTRIBUTING.md documents the code review rules: what is checked (scope; tests, with failing-first regression tests; `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint` green; the security rules for requireUser, visibility helpers, bound SQL, textContent and no secrets; allow-list input validation; no new CodeQL, Semgrep, Gitleaks or audit findings; docs, translations and CHANGELOG updated) and what's acceptable (all six points hold and CI is green). It states openly that today the one maintainer does all reviews.
two_person_review_justification: Fewer than 50% of changes are reviewed by someone other than the author. The project has one human maintainer who writes or directs (with AI agents) and merges nearly all changes, and the main branch has no branch protection or required reviews. Automated review bots (CodeRabbit, Sourcery, Aikido, Codacy, Claude Code review) comment on pull requests, but they aren't people.
build_reproducible_justification: URL: https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum/blob/main/docs/release-checklist.md#reproducing-the-build — The build can be reproduced. The only built file is the worker bundle, made with esbuild through Wrangler, with all tool versions pinned in pnpm-lock.yaml (installed with --frozen-lockfile). Building the same commit twice into different output folders gave a byte-identical worker.js (checked on v5.30.0, 2026-11-22); only the folder path in the source map and Wrangler's timestamped README differ, and neither is deployed. The commit hash is passed at deploy time, not baked into the bundle. The documented steps let anyone rebuild a tagged release and compare hashes. No independent third party has reported doing so yet.
test_statement_coverage90_justification: Statement coverage is below 90%. Node's built-in coverage (`node --test --experimental-test-coverage`) measured 88.71% line coverage, standing in for statements, on v5.30.0 (d84e01f) on 2026-11-22. Getting above 90% is a goal in ROADMAP.md.
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Branch coverage is 88.86%, measured with Node's built-in free coverage tool (`node --test --experimental-test-coverage`) on v5.30.0 (d84e01f) on 2026-11-22, across 1,188 tests with 0 failures.
hardened_site_justification: URL: https://wempos-forum.com — All project sites send the key hardening headers with strict values (checked with curl on 2026-11-22). https://wempos-forum.com sends Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self' ... frame-ancestors 'none'), Strict-Transport-Security max-age=31536000, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and X-Frame-Options (SAMEORIGIN on the HTML shell, DENY from the worker's header set), and static assets get the same headers. The repository and download site, https://github.com/Wempo-s-Silly-Projects/wempos-forum, sends CSP, HSTS (includeSubDomains), nosniff and X-Frame-Options: deny. There's no separate download site.
security_review_justification: No security review meeting this bar has been done yet. There are documented reviews of each batch of releases (docs/security-reviews/2026-11-21-v5.20-v5.23.md and 2026-11-21-v5.24-v5.27.md), but AI agents did them for the maintainer, and they cover only the changes in each batch. No review so far has looked at the whole system against the security requirements (docs/security-requirements.md) and the security boundary (docs/assurance-case.md). Commissioning a whole-system review is the next step.
